title: mcp: describe_object returns no select options, defaults or validation rules, so agents fill forms by trial and error
body:
Filing category: ① product defect.
reach: public entry `/api/v1/mcp` `tools/call describe_object`, measured on `objectos-ee` (cloud `ff373e02`, framework `d7c3d44e`) and on a maintainer-provided environment.
Batch-of: 15 cards filed together from one MCP capability test session (2026-11-11; 6 in cloud, 9 in objectstack).

## Business reason

`describe_object` is the tool an MCP agent reads before `create_record`. Without the allowed values it guesses, gets refused, and retries — every agent, on every select field.

## What happens

`describe_object` answers each field as `{ name, type, label, required }` only. For a `select` field it gives no `options`; no `defaultValue`; no validation rules; system fields (`created_at`, `owner_id`, `organization_id` …) carry no `readonly` flag, so they look writable.

Measured: an agent read `leave_type: select, required` and sent `leave_type: "年假"` (the label) → `VALIDATION_FAILED: 请假类型 must be one of: annual, sick, personal`; second call with `annual` succeeded. The same environment's `describe_metadata(type:'object')` (cloud build-door tool, only on `metadata:write` connections) does return options, defaults, validations and `readonly` — a data-only connection has no way to read them.

## Expected

`describe_object` returns, per field, what a write needs: `options` (value + label) for select-like fields, `defaultValue`, `readonly`/`system`, and the object's validation rules (or at least their messages), under the caller's FLS.

Reader who acts: the seat that owns `packages/mcp` (`mcp-http-tools.ts` describe tool).
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue describe_object options select mcp` → 4 hits (#28715 validate_expression, #27377 sweep, #25815 QA run); none on describe_object's shape.
